reader.requirement: DATE-OF-INTEGER returns the Gregorian date equivalent of argument-1, a positive integer number of days after 1600-12-31, for every such integer (no upper bound on the year at 1985) and every argument form an integer arithmetic expression allows.

edition-consulted.switches: the catalog's D8 edition window (IntroducedIn 85 for the 1989 module rows): the function is admitted at --std 85
DialectBehaviors.IsActive(IntegerDateFormBounded, year): inactive at 85, so BoundIntrinsicCall.IntegerDateFormUnbounded is true
renders `unbounded: true` into the CobolDate call when IntegerDateFormUnbounded

reader.edition-search: grep of IntrinsicBinder, IntrinsicRenderer, CobolDate and DialectBehavior for Edition, DialectLevel, DialectBehavior, IntegerDateForm, ConstructRegistry
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 the integer date form is unbounded above (day 3,067,672 is 10000-01-01); from 2002 it ends at 3,067,671 and a larger argument is an incorrect value (0)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers 1601..9999 and the three leap branches with literal arguments; not years past 9999 (the 1985 arm), nor signed, COMP, packed, subscripted or expression arguments

probes.expected: proleptic Gregorian count with 1601-01-01 = day 1, every value checked against Python datetime; year 10000 representable at 1985 (the 1989 module bounds the year below only, §1989:A.2.16.3 AR1)
1985 admits years past 9999; 2002 and later end the integer date form at 3,067,671

probes.printed: COBOL1627 refuses DATE-OF-INTEGER(SC) with SC PIC 9(7)V99, and INTEGER-OF-DAY(16000366 / 10)
probes.expected: 1989 A.2.2 argument type (4): an integer argument is an arithmetic expression which always results in an integer value; the refusal matches though its message cites §2023:15.3

probes.printed: COBOL0900: a numeric or integer function-identifier where an identifier is written requires COBOL-2002
probes.expected: 1989: an integer function may be used only in an arithmetic expression, so the 8-digit device form of DATE-OF-INTEGER is unreachable at 85

reader.notes: One proleptic Gregorian day count (400-year cycle arithmetic) whose 1985 arm is unbounded above through DialectBehavior IntegerDateFormBounded; every probed value matched an independent calendar computation, including 10000-01-01 and 10000-02-29 at 85. An out-of-range argument returns 0, within 1989's undefined result (A.2.2).

refuter.evidence: Read §1989:A.2.12.3 AR1 (positive integer, no upper bound), A.1.2.2 and A.2.2 (out-of-constraint argument: result undefined), A.2.3 (integer function only in an arithmetic expression) and CobolDate.cs#DateOfInteger/YearAndDayOf/InIntegerDateForm (unbounded arm at 85).
